# cutesdr

**Small demodulator and spectrum display for networked receivers**

- **Version recorded:** 1.20
- **Categories:** `sdr-receivers`
- **Upstream:** <http://www.rfspace.com/RFSPACE/OtherApps.html>

## What it does

Displays a spectrum and waterfall and demodulates AM, FM, SSB and CW from an RFSPACE networked receiver or a compatible sample stream. It was written as a demonstration of the DSP techniques as much as a program to use, and the source is correspondingly readable.

## Why you would want it

Two reasons and they pull in different directions. If you have RFSPACE hardware -- SDR-IQ, SDR-IP, NetSDR -- it is a direct client. If you do not, it is one of the clearest worked examples of receiver DSP in C++ that exists, which is a different kind of useful.

## Before it will work

RFSPACE hardware or a compatible stream. It does not speak SoapySDR, so it will not open an arbitrary dongle.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install cutesdr --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `cutesdr`

## Known problems

Narrow hardware support is the main limit and it is by design. The project has not moved in a long time; Qt has moved several times underneath it. For general SDR listening on ordinary hardware, gqrx or SDR++ are the right tools and this is not.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade

Moe Wheatley, AE4JY, via RFSPACE's applications page. There is no issue tracker.
